title: Case Processing SOP for Spleen Samples
author: Marda Jorgensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bc3kiykw
materials: Sample Archiving: a. All materials obtained for this program will be inventoried by the University of Florida Tissue Mapping Center (UF TMC) and archived in the Organ Processing and Pathology Core (OPPC) until use. b. Samples will be released for use or shipped to collaborator(s) upon request by the Principle Investigator.

steps.title: Assign case number
steps.instruction: Create a case number using the template YY‑NNN where YY is the two‑digit year and NNN is a sequential three‑digit number starting at 001.

steps.title: Generate sample labels
steps.instruction: Print or hand‑write labels for all cassettes, cryomolds, and containers using permanent ink or a cassette printer.

substeps.instruction: Cassettes: Line 1 – Case ID + sample‑type abbreviation; Line 2 – block number (coordinate region followed by lateral‑to‑medial position).
Cryomolds: Same Line 1; Line 2 – same as cassette plus “FX” if the mold will receive fixed frozen tissue; apply label to the bottom of the mold.
Dishes/containers: Print Case ID + sample‑type abbreviation (and common coordinate location if relevant).

steps.title: Record processing data
steps.instruction: Enter all required fields on the Case Worksheet form (case ID, date received, shipment anomalies, processing start/end times, staff, tissues received, aliquot types and numbers, tissue‑quality notes) and take photographs of the organ from all angles.

steps.title: Dissect spleen tissue
steps.instruction: Perform tissue dissection while maintaining orientation and documenting each step.

substeps.instruction: Photograph the intact organ with the hilum on the left and the inferior end at the top.
Excise a 0.5 cm cube from an interior, non‑coordinate region for RNA QC, place it in a sterile vial and flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen using RNase‑free conditions.

Cut 1 cm‑thick cross‑sectional slabs from the designated Common Coordinate regions; slide each slab slightly to the right of the residual organ and photograph the origin location using a ruler or grid.

Place each slab with the superior‑pole surface up, rotate until the hilum is at the 12 o’clock position, and cut a 1 cm‑wide strip through the centre of the slab, photographing the position before cutting.
Divide each strip into 1 cm × 1 cm × 1 cm tissue blocks (1 cm³); use a 1 cm × 1 cm matrix if helpful, photograph the cuts, and keep blocks in the recorded order and orientation.

steps.title: Fix blocks for NBF
steps.instruction: Place each 1 cm³ block designated for neutral‑buffered formalin (NBF) into its labeled cassette, immerse in NBF at room temperature with mild agitation using at least 20 mL fixative per cassette.

substeps.instruction: After 20–24 hours, transfer cassettes to 70 % ethanol and process within 3 days.

steps.title: Fix blocks for PFA
steps.instruction: Place each 1 cm³ block designated for 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) into its labeled cassette, immerse in 4 % PFA at room temperature with mild agitation using at least 20 mL fixative per cassette.

substeps.instruction: After 20–24 hours, transfer cassettes to 70 % ethanol and process within 3 days.

steps.title: Prepare frozen OCT blocks
steps.instruction: For blocks labeled for FX frozen OCT, immerse in 4 % PFA (≥20 mL per cassette) as above, then follow the embedding SOP (https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.basniede).

substeps.instruction: For fresh OCT, place the block into a labeled OCT‑filled cryomold, embed according to SOP (https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcwsixee), and transport the frozen block on dry ice.

steps.title: Process blocks for CLARITY
steps.instruction: Place the designated 1 cm³ block into 4 % PFA using a minimum fixative‑to‑tissue volume ratio of 20:1; fix for 20–24 hours at room temperature with gentle agitation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the fixed tissue to hydrogel solution and incubate for 5 days at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare blocks for 10X analysis
steps.instruction: Place the designated 1 cm³ block into a 50 mL tube containing 25 mL complete DMEM/F12 media and store the tube in a refrigerator (≈4 °C) until the sample is released for downstream isolation.

steps.title: Handle collaboration samples
steps.instruction: If the block is to be used for a collaboration project, identify “protocol B” on the worksheet and follow the external lab’s provided protocol.
